title: Factor the marketing site into its own private repository
description:
Chatticus is public and MIT-licensed: clone it, deploy it, run it. Anthus also
operates it as a paid service. Those are different concerns, and today they
share one repository and one web application.

`web/` serves marketing (`/`, `/features/*`, `/contact/*`, `/waitlist/*`,
`/beta`) and the product workspace (`/chat`, `/auth`) from one static export,
one bucket, one distribution, one pipeline. In production a single distribution
answers on both `chattic.us` and `hey.chattic.us`, with a CloudFront function
rewriting `/` to `/chat/index.html` when the Host is the app domain.

This epic ends with **two repositories, not three**:

| | Public AnthusAI/Chattic.us | Private marketing/SaaS repo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owns | Organization lifecycle, control plane, product app, CDK for the deployable product | Account (Stripe customer, setup fee, subscription, payment state), marketing site |
| Knows about | nothing downstream | organization ids, deployment targets |
| Billing code | none, ever | all of it |

The dependency direction is forced rather than chosen: a public repository can
never depend on a private one. So the public repo doubles as the shared
design-system package and the private marketing repo consumes it. No third
repository and no publish step.

**Decisions already taken:**

- The shared package is the main repo itself, consumed by branch tarball,
  always current, no version pinning. npm cannot install a subdirectory of a
  git repo, so the whole repo is the package and the root `package.json` gains
  an `exports` map. Non-reproducible marketing builds are accepted.
- Marketing Gherkin moves with the marketing site and keeps `behave`.
- The marketing distribution gets its own `/api*` behavior to the same
  thin-turn Lambda, so form posts stay same-origin. No CORS.
- The marketing CDK stack lives in the private repo with its own OIDC role.
- Marketing gets production only, matching today's asymmetry.

**Done when:** `chattic.us` serves marketing from its own deployment,
`hey.chattic.us/` serves the workspace, and this repository contains no
marketing routes, components, or specs.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Epic complete. AnthusAI/Chattic.us-web created and live: marketing site (home, beta, contact, features, waitlist, blog, wiki, legal pages) fully migrated, its own CDK app deployed (S3 + CloudFront + /api* same-origin proxy to this repo's production thin-turn Lambda, resolved via SSM/CFN-export at deploy time, not build-coupled). AnthusAI/Chattic.us renamed to AnthusAI/Chatticus (OIDC trust hardened first, verified before and after via real production deploys). Apex cutover executed: chattic.us serves marketing from the new distribution, hey.chattic.us/dev.chattic.us/staging.chattic.us all serve only the product workspace. All marketing code, specs, and now-dead CI weight removed from this repo, including 4 feature files (blog/footer/nav/wiki) that landed mid-project and were caught during cleanup rather than missed. Two backend behaviors that only had marketing-UI-driven coverage got replacement specs (contact_api.feature, a waitlist UTM scenario) before the old cross-repo scenarios were deleted.

Final verification, all live: chattic.us, www.chattic.us, hey.chattic.us, dev.chattic.us, staging.chattic.us all 200. Same-origin /api waitlist and contact POSTs confirmed against the real production backend through the marketing distribution. No stripe references anywhere in this repo. This repo: behave 73/418/2502, pytest 562, infra 128 tests, all green. Marketing repo: behave 9/49/210, 34 unit tests, all green.
